frozen_candidate_root_contribution: ع س ر marks the adverse pole of a Quran-internal ease/difficulty axis: the condition or quality of being hard-going, difficult to do, bear, or afford — the marked, dispreferred antonym of يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة (ease). Across its derivational family the nucleus is packaged as an abstract mass-noun (عُسْر), a concrete circumstance of straitened means (عُسْرَة), a lexicalized hard course/destiny (عُسْرَى), an adjective 'hard-to-undergo' fixed to the Day (عَسِير/عَسِر), and a reciprocal verb of mutual impasse (تَعَاسَرَ). The distinctive shading beyond bare 'not-easy' — burdensome constraint borne against capacity, relievable, and party-relative — is representative but leans partly on co-text, so it is not generalized to full root strength.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root ع س ر is the Quran's word-family for hardship and difficulty. Its meaning is anchored by the text itself, which repeatedly pairs it with its opposite يُسْر (ease): God wills ease for you and not hardship (2:185), after hardship comes ease (65:7), with hardship is ease (94:5-6), and a debtor in hardship waits for ease of means (2:280). It covers abstract hardship, financial straitness, a hard Day of Judgment, a hard destiny, and two people making things mutually difficult. It is never permanent, never something God endorses, and it is relative to who bears it.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: NOT impossibility or permanence (relieved by / accompanied by yusr: 65:7 بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا, 94:5-6 مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا). NOT the act or agent of imposing hardship (18:73 separates عُسْرًا from تُرْهِقْنِى, rhq). NOT spatial narrowness/constriction (65:6 separates تَعَاسَرْتُمْ from لِتُضَيِّقُوا۟, Dyq) nor harm (from تُضَآرُّوهُنَّ, Drr). NOT intrinsic or universal — party-relative (25:26 عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَسِيرًا, hard specifically upon the disbelievers). NOT physical hardness/solidity/strength. NOT in itself a moral evil (2:185 the pole God does not will; 92:10 moral loading attaches to the agent's prior stinginess, not to عسر as such). NOT a fixed wealth-class label (even عُسْرَة frames difficulty of means, opposed to مَيْسَرَة).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 92:10:2:3 «فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ» — the verb نُيَسِّر (to ease/facilitate, root ي س ر) takes ٱلْعُسْرَىٰ (hardship) as its goal: 'We will ease him toward hardship.' On a naive reading of عسر as simply 'the opposite of ease,' easing-toward-hardship is self-contradictory, placing the two anchoring antonyms in one clause. It survives only because ٱلْعُسْرَىٰ is here lexicalized as a substantive 'the hard course/destiny' (mirroring ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ at 92:7), with يسّر operating on the manner of arrival, not the destination. It does not disprove the nucleus but exposes that the elative form is partly lexicalized and that the yusr-antonymy is a systemic pairing rather than a live compositional negation.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Two related competitors cap the grade below STRONG. (1) 'Thin-antonym': ع س ر carries nothing distinctive beyond being the lexicalized negative slot on the ease-axis, and the 'burdensome constraint / hard-going' nuance is leaked from co-textual neighbors (رهق 18:73, ضيّق 65:6, insolvency 2:280) rather than from the root itself — the only feature recurring with the root as such is the yusr-antonymy. (2) 'Constriction/straitness' rather than 'difficulty', locally seductive in عُسْرَة (2:280, 9:117) and تَعَاسَرْتُمْ (65:6, adjacent to تُضَيِّقُوا۟). This second competitor loses because the Quran's own paired antonym is consistently يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة (ease/facility), never a breadth-word like سَعَة, and it under-fits the ADJ Day-class and the abstract عُسْر/يُسْر pairs — but it remains a real secondary shading localized to the concrete sub-domain. Neither competitor can be excluded on Quran-internal evidence alone, which forbids grading the distinctive nucleus above MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge that a single nucleus (hardship / hard-going, the marked antonym of yusr) is Quran-internally anchored, not imported: the text supplies the explicit antonym يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة across 2:185, 2:280, 65:7, 92:7↔10, 94:5-6, with morphological mirroring (عُسْر/يُسْر, عُسْرَى/يُسْرَى). No occurrence resists the coarse meaning, so the result is PREFERRED, not UNRESOLVED — the classes are bridged by the shared, explicitly textual ease-axis, not forced. However STRONG/UNIVERSAL is not warranted: (a) the distinctive content beyond 'the adverse pole' is thin and leans on co-textual neighbors, so the thin-antonym/constriction competitors cannot be excluded internally; (b) partly-lexicalized nominal sub-classes exist — عُسْرَة (concrete material straitness) and the elative عُسْرَى as a destiny-noun (92:10) — distinct from the bare masdar; (c) the sole verb تَعَاسَرَ (65:6) is a morphologically distinct reciprocal-agentive singleton that extends rather than instantiates the state/quality nucleus and cannot be validated at n=1. Per the contract, these resistant/extendable sub-classes cap strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE (DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY). Analyst B's STRONG/ROOT-GENERAL over-reaches on exactly the distinctiveness the contract flags; Analysts A and C are correct to cap.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Feminine elative عُسْرَى = a nominalized/lexicalized 'hard course, adverse outcome, hard destiny', mirroring ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ (92:7).
clusters.classification_rationale: In «فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ» the ease-verb يسّر takes عُسْرَى as goal, which is only coherent if عُسْرَى is a substantive destination rather than a live 'difficulty'. On-nucleus (hardness) but the level of abstraction (task-difficulty → destiny) and the partial lexicalization make this a structurally distinct, singleton use.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Direct in-sura mirror with ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ (92:7) keeps it on the ease-axis; the abstraction is of level, not a drift off-nucleus.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Adjective عَسِير/عَسِر = 'hard to undergo, grievous' — party-relative hard-going, distributionally fixed to يَوْم (the Day of Judgment).
clusters.classification_rationale: All three adjectival tokens modify يَوْم (25:26 عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَسِيرًا; 54:8 يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ; 74:9 يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ). Semantically compositional ('hard' + Day), not opaque. 25:26's عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ makes the hardness party-relative, not an intrinsic property of the Day.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Uniform distribution (always the Day) is co-textual/eschatological, not a root contribution; the eschatological flavor and fear valence come from context, not from عسر itself.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form VI تَعَاسَرَ = two parties mutually reaching an impasse / making things difficult for each other over nursing terms.
clusters.classification_rationale: The sole verb and the only agentive, reciprocal token (65:6 وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُۥٓ أُخْرَىٰ): hardship enacted between parties, not merely suffered. A state/quality nucleus reaches this reading only by Form-VI morphology — a derivational extension external to the nucleus — and cannot be distributionally validated at n=1. Bridgeable ('mutually enact عسر'), so not resistant, but structurally atypical. The competing 'constriction/impasse' reading is locally strongest here (adjacent ضيق, no يسر antonym in-clause; the yusr anchor appears only in the next verse 65:7).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Thematic bridge to the yusr-capped 65:7 in the same sura keeps it on-nucleus, but the agentive-reciprocal mode is not natively covered by the stative gloss.

reconciliation.rationale: Resolved by reading عُسْرَى as a lexicalized substantive 'hard course/destiny' (mirroring ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ 92:7), with يسّر operating on the manner of arrival. Remains on the ease-axis; downgraded from resistant to structural (partial lexicalization), not forced into unity nor left resistant.

Bridged to the nucleus as 'mutually enacting عسر (hardship)', thematically capped by the yusr of the very next verse (65:7). The reciprocity is a Form-VI derivational effect, not a second lexical meaning; kept as a structural atypicality rather than a resistant seam.

No occurrence refutes the nucleus, so status is not FAILED.

candidate_root_contribution: ع س ر marks the adverse pole of a Quran-internal ease/difficulty axis: the condition or quality of being hard-going, difficult to do, bear, or afford — the marked, dispreferred antonym of يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة (ease). Across its derivational family the nucleus is packaged as an abstract mass-noun (عُسْر), a concrete circumstance of straitened means (عُسْرَة), a lexicalized hard course/destiny (عُسْرَى), an adjective 'hard-to-undergo' fixed to the Day (عَسِير/عَسِر), and a reciprocal verb of mutual impasse (تَعَاسَرَ). The distinctive shading beyond bare 'not-easy' — burdensome constraint borne against capacity, relievable, and party-relative — is representative but leans partly on co-text, so it is not generalized to full root strength.

layer_attribution.derivation: Morphology packages one nucleus into a derivational family: masdar عُسْر (abstract quality), state-noun عُسْرَة (+tā', concrete circumstance), feminine elative عُسْرَى (substantivized course/destiny), adjective عَسِير/عَسِر ('hard'), and Form VI تَعَاسَرَ (reciprocity). Packaging conditions realization without severing meaning, but -at concreteness, elative substantivization, and Form-VI reciprocity are morphological effects, not separate lexical meanings.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Two partly-lexicalized nominal sub-classes are recognized: عُسْرَة (material straitness of means, 2:280/9:117) and the elative عُسْرَى as a destiny-noun (92:10). These, plus the Form-VI singleton, are why the claim is graded DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY / REPRESENTATIVE rather than ROOT_GENERALIZATION / UNIVERSAL.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Fear/eschatological valence (ADJ Day-class), financial framing (عُسْرَة), imposition (رهق, 18:73), narrowing/harm (ضيّق/ضرّ, 65:6), and moral loading (stinginess, 92:8-9) are co-textual and must NOT be promoted into the root claim; the root contributes only the adverse hardship pole.

evidence_basis.statement: The sole verb and the only agentive, reciprocal token (65:6 وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُۥٓ أُخْرَىٰ): hardship enacted between parties, not merely suffered. A state/quality nucleus reaches this reading only by Form-VI morphology — a derivational extension external to the nucleus — and cannot be distributionally validated at n=1. The competing 'constriction/impasse' reading is locally strongest here (adjacent ضيق, no يسر antonym in-clause; the yusr anchor appears only in the next verse 65:7).

hard_case_representation.rationale: The core nucleus is not resistant — the explicit, repeated yusr/maysara antonymy bridges every class, so no occurrence is finally RESISTANT. Two genuine hard cases remain as structural pressure: 92:10 (lexicalized elative paradox, ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY) and 65:6 (agentive-reciprocal Form-VI singleton, STRUCTURAL_ATYPICALITY). Both are derived from and resolved against the packet evidence rather than persisted as unresolved resistance.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: The distinctive 'burdensome constraint / hard-going, party-relative, relievable' content is shown to be entirely co-textual leakage, such that ع س ر contributes nothing beyond the bare lexicalized negative slot of the ease-axis — or, conversely, a second unbridged lexical meaning (spatial constriction) is established for عُسْرَة/تَعَاسَرَ independent of any yusr/maysara pairing.
rejection_condition.search_location: 18:73 (رهق), 65:6 (ضيّق/ضرّ), 2:280 and 9:117 (عُسْرَة), 92:10 (عُسْرَى), and the ADJ Day-class 25:26/54:8/74:9 — plus every co-occurrence of يُسْر/مَيْسَرَة with the root.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Strip the co-textual neighbors (رهق, ضيّق, ضرّ, insolvency framing) and test whether the constraint/hard-going nuance still recurs with the root as such; separately test whether any عُسْرَة/تَعَاسَرَ occurrence carries 'constriction of space' without an available ease-antonym reading.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish root contribution from (a) neighboring roots ي س ر, ر ه ق, ض ي ق, ض ر ر supplying the sense; (b) morphological packaging (-at concreteness, elative substantivization, Form-VI reciprocity) masquerading as distinct lexical meaning; (c) eschatological co-text (the Day) attaching fear valence.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If the distinctive nuance is pure leakage, the claim collapses to the coarse yusr-antonym only and result_strength/claim_scope for the distinctive account must be dropped; if a second unbridged constriction meaning is established, research_state must move to UNRESOLVED (multi-class) rather than a single DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY nucleus.

reopen_conditions: If a re-analysis of 65:6 تَعَاسَرْتُمْ establishes 'mutual spatial constriction' as its lexical meaning independent of the ease-axis (e.g., by tightening the tie to adjacent لِتُضَيِّقُوا۟, ض ي ق), reopen to test a split between a hardship nucleus and a constriction sub-sense.

If 92:10 ٱلْعُسْرَىٰ and 92:7 ٱلْيُسْرَىٰ are shown to be a frozen lexicalized pair with no live compositional link to the masdar عُسْر/يُسْر, reopen to reclassify the elative as its own LEXICALIZED_CLASS.
If the ADJ Day-class (25:26, 54:8, 74:9) is argued to be an opaque eschatological lexeme rather than compositional 'hard + Day', reopen to test whether عَسِير has drifted into a distinct fixed sense.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The coarse nucleus (hardship, marked antonym of yusr) passes with zero failing occurrences. Formal falsification is recorded as NOT_RUN rather than PASSED because distinctiveness_ok is not satisfied: the distinctive nuance beyond 'the adverse pole' cannot be shown Quran-internally to be independent of co-textual neighbors (thin-antonym/constriction competitors survive), and two structurally atypical occurrences (92:10 lexicalized elative, 65:6 Form-VI singleton) extend the nucleus without validating it. No occurrence refutes the nucleus, so status is not FAILED.
